title: Smiling Face with Tear Emoji 🥲 Meaning: Bittersweet
description: The smiling face with tear emoji 🥲 smiles while a single tear falls: bittersweet pride, brave-face sadness, and “I'm fine” that nobody believes. See real examples.
summary: The 🥲 smiling face with tear shows a gentle smile and one tear rolling down the cheek. It means mixed feelings: happy and sad at once, or smiling through pain. People use it for bittersweet moments, proud tears, and, very often, wry jokes about putting on a brave face.
meaning: Some feelings do not sort neatly into happy or sad, and 🥲 exists for them. A child leaving for college, the last episode of a loved show, a friend moving away for a dream job: the smile is real and so is the tear. In these moments the emoji says “I'm glad, and it hurts a little.”

It also covers being moved. A surprise party, a kind note, or a wedding speech can bring a tear to a smiling face, and 🥲 captures that swell of gratitude. Here it overlaps with 🥹, the face holding back tears. The difference is that on 🥲 the tear has already escaped.

The most widespread use online is ironic. 🥲 is the face of someone insisting they are okay when they obviously are not. “Paid rent, account is at $4 🥲” and “they said they'd call back 🥲” use the smile as a thin cover over disappointment. It arrived in 2020 and was taken up quickly for this kind of rueful humor about everyday setbacks.

What keeps it from being merely sad is the acceptance in it. Unlike a crying face, 🥲 is not asking to be rescued. It reports a hurt and shrugs at the same time. That makes it a comfortable way to mention real disappointment lightly, though it can also mask something heavier, so it is worth a second look when a friend uses it repeatedly.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Used for small defeats and tender moments alike. It softens bad news about yourself so the other person does not have to worry: “didn't get the job 🥲.” It also responds to sweet messages when you feel touched. Tone depends on the sentence; with good news it is happy tears, with bad news a brave face.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: A fixture of self-deprecating humor. It labels videos and posts about being broke, single, overworked, or forgotten, always with a note of “it's fine, I'm fine.” It also appears sincerely under nostalgic content and emotional milestones such as graduations and farewell tours.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: Usually about circumstances, not about you. They might be joking about a rough day or sad that plans fell through. If it follows “wish you were here” or a canceled date, it shows disappointment at missing you, which is a good sign. It is not flirtatious in itself.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Common among colleagues for shared, low-stakes misery: a canceled holiday party, a bug found late on Friday. It signals that you are taking a setback in good humor. Avoid it when reporting serious problems, where it may seem to make light of them or to hint at distress you have not explained.

examples.text: Dropped her off at the dorm today 🥲
examples.meaning: Proud and sad together as a child leaves home.

examples.text: Studied all week and still got a C 🥲
examples.meaning: Disappointed but taking it on the chin.
Touched to the point of tears.

examples.meaning: Pretending not to mind being left out.

combos.meaning: Things keep going wrong and the sender keeps smiling.
Heartbroken but trying to be gracious about it.

confusedWith.difference: 🥹 has big watery eyes with tears that have not fallen. It expresses being overwhelmed by cuteness, gratitude, or pride. 🥲 has let one tear go and carries more sadness and resignation. 🥹 is touched; 🥲 is bittersweet.
😂 is laughing so hard it cries, with an open grin and two tears. 🥲 has a small closed smile and one tear, and is not about humor. Mixing them up can make a sad message look like laughter.
😥 frowns with a drop on its brow and shows worry or disappointment with some relief. It does not smile. 🥲 keeps a smile on, which is what gives it the brave-face, mixed-emotion meaning.

avoid: Don't use it to respond to someone else's serious loss, where a smile of any kind is out of place.
Avoid it as your only way of signaling real distress, because readers often take it as a joke.
Skip it in formal messages; the irony does not translate well.
design: A yellow face with a soft closed smile, open eyes, and a single tear on one cheek. Eyebrows, where shown, are slightly raised. The tear sits below the eye on the right side of the image on most platforms. Apple, Google, Samsung, and Microsoft are closely aligned; the main variation is the size of the tear and how wide the smile is.

faqs.a: Both, by design. It can mean happy tears, as when you are touched or proud, or sadness behind a smile, as when you are disappointed and coping. The message around it shows which side is stronger.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 🥲 and 🥹?
faqs.a: 🥹 is about to cry from emotion, usually positive: something is adorable or moving. 🥲 has already shed a tear and often implies loss or resignation. Use 🥹 for “that's so sweet” and 🥲 for “that's bittersweet.”

faqs.q: What does 🥲 mean from a guy or a girl?
faqs.a: They are feeling something mixed or putting a brave face on a letdown. It is frequently self-deprecating humor. If it is about not seeing you, they are a little sad about it. It does not have a gender-specific meaning.
Often it is wry more than sarcastic. People use it to joke about their own misfortune, with a smile that fools no one. It is seldom aimed at another person, so it rarely comes across as hostile.
It was approved in 2020 as part of Emoji 13.0. It spread quickly because it captured the mix of coping and sadness that many people wanted to express.
